by JESSICA A. BOTELHO | The National News Desk

TOPICS:

WASHINGTON (TNND) — President Donald Trump said he is prepared to keep Todd Blanche as acting attorney general if the Senate does not confirm him to the permanent post, while renewing criticism of two Republican senators he blamed for stalling the nomination.

The president on Saturday singled out Sens. John Cornyn, of Texas, and Thom Tillis, of North Carolina, claiming they both opposed Blanche after he declined to endorse their political campaigns.

Trump asserted that Cornyn "lost" and Tillis "quit," referring to their political fortunes, and accused them of standing in the way of Blanche's confirmation.

He went on to praise Blanche as as "a voice of reason."

Trump also pledged to push for passage of "the Anti-Weaponization Bill," legislation he said is intended to address what he has repeatedly described as the political misuse of the justice system during the Biden administration.

The social media post comes a few days after Trump said he might withdraw Blanche’s nomination until Tillis and John Cornyn are out of office.

Trump on Friday said he doesn't blame Cornyn for stalling Blanche's nomination, adding that he would do the same thing if he were in Cornyn’s shoes.

Blanche, a former federal prosecutor and defense attorney, has served as acting attorney general while awaiting Senate action on his nomination. The Senate had not yet voted on his confirmation as of Friday.

Trump has frequently accused the Biden administration of weaponizing the Department of Justice Department against political opponents, allegations that former administration officials have denied.
